theorem_title: Lemma 2.7 — hashing preserves expansion uniformly in the preliminary matrix
formal_statement:
namespace ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch

open Filter
/-- Lemma 2.7. The little-o envelope is uniform over all admissible preliminary outputs. -/
theorem hash_expansion (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / 2)
    (g : ∀ n, Geometry (dimension ε) n) :
    ∃ δ : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ n, 0 ≤ δ n) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n => δ n * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / ε)) atTop (nhds 0) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ s : Forms (g n).F (dimension ε) (arity ε),
        PreliminaryGood ε n (g n) s →
        uniformProb (fun h : Hashes (g n).F (arity ε) (buckets ε n) =>
          ¬ Expanding (combined (g n) s h) (1 - ε) (arity ε) ((n : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε))) ≤ δ n := by sorry

end ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch
natural_language_statement:
Fix $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and the construction parameters. There is a nonnegative function $\delta(n)$, independent of the particular preliminary output, such that
$$\delta(n)n^{1/\varepsilon}\longrightarrow0.$$
For all sufficiently large $n$ and every fixed preliminary output $A$ satisfying $|\Gamma_A(S)|\ge(k-d+1)|S|$ for every $|S|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}$, independent uniform all-functions hashes satisfy
$$\Pr_h[G\text{ is not }(1-\varepsilon,k,n^{1-\varepsilon})\text{-expanding}]\le\delta(n).$$
Exact row weight is part of the expansion conclusion. No preliminary output satisfying the source's condition is removed, and no conditioning on hash success is performed.

This supplies the uniform little-o failure estimate for the column-combining step.

Differences from the source:
- encoding: condition on any A satisfying Lemma 2.6 with failure o(n^{−1/ε}) → a single nonnegative little-o envelope chosen before n and before every admissible preliminary seed; reason: this makes the source proof’s uniformity in A explicit and prevents output-dependent asymptotic constants
- encoding: uniform independent functions h_i → the uniform law on the complete finite product of all hash tables; reason: every value of every layer hash remains independent and uniform
